articles.title: AFCAT 2 exam city intimation slip 2026 released at afcat.cdac.in: Direct link to download here
articles.summary: The AFCAT 2 exam city intimation slip for 2026 has been released and is available for download on afcat.cdac.in. Aspirants appearing for the Air Force Common Admission Test can access their slips directly from the official website. This notification is vital for candidates to check their allotted exam city, enabling them to plan their travel and logistics well in advance for this crucial defence entrance examination.

articles.title: Ren'py malware verification.
articles.summary: An individual reported accidentally downloading and executing a 'Ren'py malware installer.exe' file, prominently featuring an anime girl icon. Despite running the suspicious program, no visible loading or immediate activity was observed, raising concerns about its unseen effects. This incident underscores critical personal cybersecurity vigilance and the deceptive tactics employed by malware, relevant for digital awareness.

articles.title: Russia charges Telegram founder with aiding terrorism
articles.summary: Russia has charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity, alleging Ukrainian spies use the messaging app to organize attacks within Russia. This move by Moscow underscores ongoing geopolitical tensions and the weaponization of digital platforms in the conflict, highlighting concerns over communication security and state-backed cyber operations amidst the protracted Russia-Ukraine war.

articles.title: Air Force members don't have unqualified right to leave job at will: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has delivered a significant verdict, stating that Indian Air Force members do not possess an unqualified right to leave service at will to join civil posts. This clarifies that personnel cannot prematurely resign for civilian employment without adhering to specific regulations, reinforcing the commitment and service obligations of armed forces personnel. The ruling has implications for service conditions across the defence sector.

articles.title: Krafton have big plans for Subnautica, after the second game's once-divisive co-op "confirmed the potential to expand beyond the existing fan base"
articles.summary: Krafton, publisher of "Subnautica 2," reportedly paid a substantial earn-out to developer Unknown Worlds after losing a courtroom battle with ousted studio executives. Despite this legal and financial setback, Krafton remains highly optimistic about the ocean survival game's success. This event highlights complex business and legal dynamics within the global gaming industry.

articles.title: Jordan intercepts Iranian missiles as U.S., Saudi Arabia target militias in Iraq
articles.summary: Jordan and the U.S. military recently intercepted Iranian missiles and barrages launched in the Middle East. Jordan intercepted missiles early Wednesday, while the U.S. military reported knocking down another Iranian barrage aimed at American forces. This highlights the escalating regional tensions and the active role of various nations in maintaining security amidst ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

articles.title: End date for US submarines in WA revealed | 7.30
articles.summary: Next year, a US nuclear-powered submarine, its crew, and families, will be stationed at the Stirling naval base. This deployment signifies a significant strengthening of US naval presence and strategic partnerships. For SSB aspirants, this highlights evolving international defence cooperation, underscoring the strategic importance of naval power and alliances.

articles.title: CCIB names Goodfish Lake Business Corporation as 2026 Indigenous Business of the Year
articles.summary: The Canadian Council for Indigenous Business (CCIB) has announced Goodfish Lake Business Corporation (GFLBC) as the 2026 recipient of its prestigious Indigenous Business award. This recognition, reported from Toronto on July 29, 2026, highlights GFLBC's significant contributions and achievements within the Indigenous business sector in Canada, celebrating excellence and leadership in economic development for Indigenous communities.

articles.title: Day 1,617 of WW3. Orcistan's deputy PM claims russian refineries are "operational" again, and the fuel crisis is "stabilizing". Wildberries looks at opening warehouses in Kazakhstan to prevent UAF attacks. This is your Wednesday Ukraine War thread [News]
articles.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes have disrupted Russia's logistics network. Consequently, major e-commerce giant Wildberries is reportedly eyeing new warehouse expansion in Kazakhstan to secure its operations. This move underscores how the ongoing conflict in Ukraine is forcing businesses to adapt supply chains and operational strategies due to security risks, impacting regional commerce and logistics networks significantly.
